newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya says freed detainees to mark Ramadan.
newsitem.headline: Libya says freed detainees to mark Ramadan.

text.p: Libya has marked the start of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan by freeing a number of people held for alleged corruption, the official Libyan news agency JANA said.
JANA, monitored in Tunis, said on Thursday night that justice authorities had taken the decision on the release to mark Ramadan which started in Libya on Friday.

It did not say how many people were released but said only 29 people arrested by the so-called anti-corruption committees remained in prison and that their files would be submitted to justice authorities for investigation.
Hundreds of such committees were set up last year on the order of Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to fight what they called financial and economic corruption.
Reports in the Arab press abroad had alleged that some of the committees arrested people without evidence.
